title: Amelogenesis Imperfecta and Dental Treatment Outcomes: A Comprehensive Study and Registry
summary:
Amelogenesis imperfecta (AI) is a rare genetic disorder that affects enamel formation. Individuals with AI often have sensitive teeth, an increased risk of dental caries, and both aesthetic and functional impairments. Dental treatment is complex – yet there is currently limited scientific data on long-term treatment outcomes and quality of life in patients with AI.

The aim of this study is to comprehensively assess and analyze the dental care and quality of life of individuals affected by AI over an extended period of time. This includes, for example, standardized questionnaires on oral health-related quality of life, clinical examinations, analysis of saliva, plaque, and dental hard tissues, as well as digital impressions to evaluate enamel wear.

A patient registry forms the basis for systematic long-term observation. Additional data will be collected on the oral microbiome, dietary habits, and treatment costs.

In the long term, this study aims to contribute to the development of evidence-based treatment recommendations for AI – with the goal of improving patients’ quality of life and ensuring high-quality dental care.
conditions: Hereditary disturbances in tooth structure, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name:
Patients presenting with a condition within the spectrum of Amelogenesis Imperfecta (AI)

To assess oral health-related quality of life, validated, age-appropriate questionnaires will be used: the OHIP-14 for adults and adolescents aged 18 years and older, the COHIP for children aged 8 to 17 years

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Sufficient cooperation for an intraoral examination
- Completed informed consent form signed by parents/legal guardians
- Adequate ability to perform proper oral hygiene at home (in the case of children, this must be ensured by the parents)
Exclusion criteria:
- Structural enamel anomaly of a different origin
- Participants who do not meet the inclusion criteria
- Participant withdraws informed consent
